title: Ransomware spreads from an admin workstation to clinical servers
asset: EHR application and database servers (data centre)
threat: Ransomware delivered by phishing or a malicious download
vulnerability: Admin VLAN can reach some server ports used by business apps; server backups are not offline or immutable
existing_controls: VLAN segmentation (Admin 20 and Clinical 10); least-privilege ACLs; pfSense edge firewall; nightly server backups to the data centre NAS

title: Unpatched medical devices on VLAN 50 are exploited
asset: Networked medical devices (imaging modalities and infusion pump gateways)
threat: Malware or an attacker exploiting known operating system flaws
vulnerability: Vendor-locked operating systems that IT cannot patch; no inventory of device OS and firmware versions
existing_controls: Dedicated Medical devices VLAN 50; ACLs allow only required flows to PACS and the EHR interface engine

title: Guest Wi-Fi user reaches internal systems through an ACL mistake
asset: Clinical and admin networks at both hospitals
threat: Curious or malicious guest user
vulnerability: Guest isolation depends on hand-written ACLs with no scheduled review
existing_controls: Guest VLAN 40 with an internet-only ACL; pfSense edge firewall

title: Clinic loses its primary WAN link and cannot reach the EHR
asset: Clinic access to the EHR and VoIP
threat: Carrier outage or cut fibre
vulnerability: Each clinic has a single primary circuit
existing_controls: IPsec VPN backup path over the internet; OSPF reroutes traffic to the backup path

title: Stolen or shared admin credentials used to change network devices
asset: Routers, switches and the edge firewall
threat: Attacker or former staff member with known credentials
vulnerability: Shared local admin account on network devices; no MFA for device management
existing_controls: SSH-only management; Management VLAN 99; ACLs limit who can reach device management

title: Config backups expose passwords or keys
threat: Unauthorized access to backup storage or a careless export
vulnerability: Backups sit unencrypted on a shared server; secret removal is best effort
existing_controls: Credentials kept in environment variables and never written to files; sanitize option redacts secrets

title: Intrusion goes unnoticed because logs are not reviewed
threat: Attacker activity hidden in unreviewed logs
vulnerability: Central syslog has no alert rules, so problems are only found during the weekly review
existing_controls: Central syslog (rsyslog) receives router, switch and firewall logs; weekly log review since September 2026; 1-year retention

title: Patient data intercepted between a clinic and the data centre
threat: Interception on the provincial WAN
vulnerability: Primary WAN path has no network-layer encryption; a legacy HL7 feed may not use TLS
existing_controls: IPsec (AES-256/SHA-256) on the backup path; most clinical apps use HTTPS

title: Staff look up patient records without a clinical need
threat: Insider snooping
vulnerability: No regular user access reviews; EHR audit logs are not monitored
existing_controls: Role-based EHR access through AD groups

title: Phishing leads to a compromised staff account
threat: Credential phishing
vulnerability: MFA is not enforced for all staff; no phishing awareness training
existing_controls: Email filtering at the mail provider

title: Single edge firewall fails and cuts internet and partner access
threat: Hardware or software failure
vulnerability: Only one firewall at the data centre edge
existing_controls: Config backups allow a rebuild

title: Vendor remote support access to medical devices is uncontrolled
threat: Compromised vendor account or remote access tool
vulnerability: Vendor uses an always-on remote access tool with no per-session approval or logging
existing_controls: Medical devices VLAN 50

title: Teleradiology vendor keeps a copy of images outside Canada
asset: Diagnostic images and reports (personal health information)
threat: Data held under a foreign jurisdiction without approval
vulnerability: Disaster recovery replica sits in the US; contract does not set data residency; SOC 2 report covers the US region only
existing_controls: Vendor assessment completed (reports/vendor_assessment_prairie_imaging_cloud.md)

title: Unknown device plugged into a clinic network port
threat: Visitor or staff member connecting an unmanaged device
vulnerability: Unused switch ports were left active
existing_controls: Unused ports disabled; port security on clinic access switches

title: Unauthorized physical access to clinic network equipment
threat: Tampering or theft
vulnerability: Clinic equipment sits in shared storage rooms
existing_controls: Locked network closets at both hospitals

title: Unreviewed changes weaken ACLs over time
threat: Configuration drift
vulnerability: Changes made directly on devices without a change ticket; no comparison against an approved baseline
existing_controls: Nightly config backups keep a copy of each running config

title: Loss of the directory server stops logins at all sites
asset: Windows Server AD, DNS and DHCP
threat: Server failure or corruption
vulnerability: One domain controller (also running DNS and DHCP) at the data centre only
existing_controls: Nightly server backups to the data centre NAS

title: Management traffic such as SNMP is read or altered
threat: Sniffing or spoofing on the network
vulnerability: Monitoring needs SNMP access to every device
existing_controls: SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption; Management VLAN 99; SSH only

title: No tested plan for responding to a network security incident
threat: Slow or confused response during an incident
vulnerability: No written network incident playbook; roles not agreed with clinical managers
existing_controls: IT helpdesk ticket process

title: Known vulnerabilities on servers and network devices go unfound
threat: Exploitation of published vulnerabilities
vulnerability: No scheduled vulnerability scanning
existing_controls: Vendor patch notices emailed to the infrastructure team
